## Announcements

### New dinosaur identified by Museum Paleontologists!

![Image 10](https://www.nmnaturalhistory.org/sites/default/files/Dinevenator%20by%20Sergey%20Krasovskiy_WEB%20version.jpg)

Exciting news: Paleontologists from the New Mexico Museum of Natural History & Science have identified a new genus of two-legged dinosaur that lived in New Mexico more than 70 million years ago!

Introducing _Dinevenator robustus_. Dinevenator was a troodontid, a family of bird-like dinosaurs known for having unusually large brains relative to other dinosaurs. Scientists believe Dinevenator was approximately 8 to 10 feet in body length and weighed between 150 to 300 pounds, making it one of the larger troodontids known.(Artwork by Sergey Krasovskiy)

Eligible residents should bring a driver's license or any other proof of residency to the Museum's front desk to participate during either of those periods. This includes free museum admission and entry to a show at our Planetarium.
